housing: Staffordshire Moorlands runs from the edge of Stoke-on-Trent up into the Peak District, with Leek, Biddulph and Cheadle as its towns. Leek has Victorian terraces and converted silk mills, while the hill villages have stone cottages, farmhouses and barn conversions, many off the gas grid. Private renting is low, at about one in eight households, and few properties need an HMO licence. Affordability worsened sharply between 2019 and 2024.
checkinTips: Stone cottages and farmhouses in the Peak District villages: photograph walls inside for damp, window reveals, chimney breasts and the condition of any wood burner.
Homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any septic tank or treatment plant cover.
Upland homes exposed to winter weather: check gutters, roof slates, outside pipes and any frost damage, and note any snow and ice arrangements for access.
Victorian terraces and converted mills in Leek: record the back yard, rear gate, large mill windows and any condensation marks.
Homes near the Caldon Canal and the Churnet: check ground floors and gardens for damp or signs of past flooding.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Staffordshire Moorlands District Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
